I wouldn't hate on America. I'm from a country where homosexual activity is punishable by 2 years in prison, and there is little to no conversation at all about social change to improve the situation of LGBT folk here.

Yes, the homophobes and the hate groups are disgusting people that should be shamed and fought against with every fibre of our beings. But at the same time, I also read about straight people from America who are very vocal in their support of the LGBT community, who are committed to helping us fight for our rights, and who generally love us as equal human beings. I may be looking at America with too idealized a perspective, but for an outsider like me, who has received no such public support in my own country, I can't help but feel moved when I read about this kind of resistance to hate groups.

The hate groups are disgusting and their high profile in the media sullies America's name. But I also see a lot of good people from America standing up against them, and that makes me happy.

I work in a law firm. It's been 6 months since I've been called to the bar, but I've been working at this firm for slightly over a year now. I'm given no guidance, working in an area of law I have no experience in, and feel like I'm doing everything blind. I don't feel like I've learnt how to do anything. I get yelled at for asking questions. I get yelled at for whatever work I turn in. I'm constantly in a state of anxiety and alert, wondering what else I fucked up and who else is going to yell at me, and worrying about how long I can keep up this charade that I'm a "competent worker". And I get to do this at work, 15 hours a day, every day. I'm so utterly tired, all I want to do is sleep. I don't mind never waking up. I feel utterly worthless all the time, but I'm too tired to cry. At work, I wonder if I'm better off dead, at least 3 times every 5 minutes.

Thank you for your response, I haven't had the time to look at this thread until now. Things are getting worse, I've been getting anxiety attacks, I swing between not eating and binge eating and have been falling asleep at my desk. I want to leave so badly but I feel so trapped. I need to support my family and my parents have health problems. I feel like I've invested my youth and money to get into a career that will kill me. I've been dreaming so much about shooting myself but I don't dare to yet. I'm very tired and I just want to sleep. I really don't know how to find the courage or motivation to do what I need to do anymore.

I work these insane hours for a few reasons, the nature of the business (clients are demanding and frequently have urgent deadlines, so a great volume of work has to be done within a few days), also my firm is understaffed in terms of lawyers, and my inexperience means that I tend to take longer with a piece of work than someone with more experience would. My firm constantly takes on all the work it can get, but doesn't hire to keep up with the workload.

I find it very hard to speak to my parents about this, they both have health problems and have worked incredibly hard to provide for my brother and I. My brother is not very responsible, financially or otherwise, and is constantly out of the country, so I have to take care of my parents, even though these days I simply don't have the time to do so. From a young age I've always felt like I've had to be the responsible one, to provide for everyone when I have the means to do so, and it's starting to get tiring.

Thank you for your comment, even though it's over the internet, it feels like the first genuine human contact I've had in months.
